title: Fix "inclusive inherited interfaces" to walk the inheritance chain
body: The [inherited interfaces](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-inherited-interfaces) of an interface are defined recursively: the interface it directly inherits from, plus all of *that* interface's inherited interfaces. So [inclusive inherited interfaces](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-inclusive-inherited-interfaces) should walk the whole inheritance chain. But step 3.2 advances from the fixed input |I| instead of the loop variable |interface|: > Set |interface| to the interface that |I| inherits from, if any, and null otherwise. So after the first iteration, |interface| is always |I|'s direct parent and never becomes null. The loop never ends for any interface that inherits from another. This PR changes |I| to |interface| so each iteration moves one level up the chain. The algorithm is used by: - [implements](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implements), which regular operations and attributes use to check their `this` value - [internally create a new object implementing the interface](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#internally-create-a-new-object-implementing-the-interface), which copies each ancestor's `[LegacyUnforgeable]` members onto the new instance. For example, `CustomEvent` inherits from `Event`, which has a `[LegacyUnforgeable]` attribute: ```webidl interface CustomEvent : Event { ... }; interface Event { ... [LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute boolean isTrusted; ... }; ``` Under the current text, `new CustomEvent("foo")` would never finish. With the fix, it returns an object with `isTrusted` as an own property whose value is `false`. Implementations seems to behave this way. Chrome, Firefox, and Safari pass dom/idlharness.any.js on wpt.fyi, which includes test for `new CustomEvent("foo")`. So, this might be the change to align the spec with existing behavior. *** Preview | Diff
